result.clarifying_question: What exactly would 'letting the agents ship' authorize — autonomous merge to the main branch, autonomous deployment to production, or autonomous release to end customers — and would it cover all changes or only a scoped set (e.g., internal tools or low-risk services)?
result.rationale: The request is researchable: evidence on agent reliability, failure modes, control mechanisms, and enterprise governance practice can inform a ship-autonomy decision, so abstaining is not warranted. However, 'ship' is a decision-changing ambiguity that cannot be resolved without guessing: autonomous merge, autonomous production deployment, and autonomous customer release are distinct risk regimes requiring different evidence (code-quality gates vs. deployment safety and rollback vs. release and compliance controls), and neither the request nor the domain indicates which is meant, nor whether the decision is a blanket policy change or a scoped pilot. Guessing would risk framing the wrong governance decision. One blocking clarification is therefore asked before any mission is issued; no mission, findings, or permissions are asserted, and the eventual mission will inform — not make — the ship/no-ship decision.
